alignments.note: Genitive-absolute participle rendered finite; the supplied 'when' is a rule 86 helper on the participle and the supplied object 'him' a rule 7 helper on the verb that requires it in English.
The ASV writes 'a longer time' with no preposition, so nothing answers to ἐπί; rule 36 leaves a preposition empty only where English realizes it nowhere.
Comparative adjective standing bare: the supplied determiner belongs to the noun it determines, not to the attributive adjective standing next to it.

Both the adjective and the noun are anarthrous and the ASV supplies a determiner for the phrase, so rule 58 gives 'a' to the noun, discontinuously around the adjective under rule 15, exactly as ὥραν … ἑβδόμην → 'at the seventh hour' gives 'at the … hour' to the noun. Rule 58 forbids in terms reading the determiner off English word order because it stands next to the adjective, and 18:24 already reads the same shape this way in 'an eloquent man'. Placing 'a' with 'longer' as one comparative expression is the competing reading.
Infinitive with its marker; rule 7, no conjunction governing the clause.
Negative aligned to 'not', discontinuous under rule 15.
Finite verb with its supplied subject; head on the lexical verb.

review_notes: The accepted alignment put the supplied 'a' on πλείονα. Rule 58 places a determiner supplied for an anarthrous adjective-plus-noun phrase on the noun, and 18:24 in this same chapter already does so for 'an eloquent man'; rule 24's habit requires the two to be analysed alike.
ἐπί is unrepresented: the ASV realizes it nowhere in the English phrase.
